title: California's AI provenance law binds 1M-user providers
summary: SB 942 became operative on 2 August, forcing large generative-AI providers to embed provenance data and publish a free detection tool.
body:
## A second deadline, deliberately synchronised

California's AI Transparency Act took effect on 2 August 2026, the same day the European Union's Article 50 transparency duties became applicable — an alignment written into the statute on purpose.

The law, passed as SB 942 in 2024 and substantially rewritten by AB 853 before Governor Gavin Newsom signed it on 13 October 2025, applies to providers of generative AI systems with more than one million monthly visitors or users in California. That threshold captures essentially every consumer-facing frontier model vendor operating in the state.

Covered providers must embed latent provenance data into the image, video and audio content their systems generate — information identifying the content's origin and modification history — and must make available, at no cost, a publicly accessible detection tool that reads any provenance data present in a piece of content and reports what it finds. Providers must also offer users the option of a visible, manifest disclosure.

Enforcement runs through civil actions rather than a regulator's licence power, with penalties of $5,000 per violation per day. For a service updated continuously at scale, that structure makes sustained non-compliance expensive quickly.

## What comes next

AB 853 did more than move the date. It extended the Act's architecture beyond model providers to large online platforms, generative-AI system hosting platforms and capture device manufacturers, phasing those duties in later — the hosting-platform obligation begins 1 January 2027. The clear direction is to push provenance metadata along the whole chain, from the camera that records an image to the platform that distributes it, rather than resting the entire burden on the model that generated it.

## Why it matters

There is still no federal provenance standard. Executive Order 14409, signed on 2 June 2026, gave agencies until 1 August to design a voluntary pre-release disclosure framework for frontier models; that date passed with nothing published, and the benchmarking process the order describes is classified by design, so the framework may never surface publicly in full. In its absence California is again setting the de facto US rule for how generative media must be labelled. Combined with the EU obligations that landed the same day, the two largest regulated markets for consumer AI now require the same underlying plumbing: cryptographic or metadata provenance embedded at generation time, plus a public way to check it. That is a hard engineering requirement, not a policy statement, and it applies to models served worldwide.
title_zh: 加州AI透明度法生效：百万用户级模型须标来源
summary_zh: SB 942于8月2日正式施行，要求大型生成式AI提供方在内容中嵌入来源信息，并免费提供公开的检测工具。
body_zh:
## 刻意对齐的第二个截止日

加州《AI透明度法》于2026年8月2日生效，与欧盟《AI法案》第50条透明度义务同日落地——这种时间对齐是立法时有意为之。

该法2024年以SB 942通过，其后由AB 853大幅改写，纽森州长于2025年10月13日签署。适用对象是在加州月访问量或用户数超过100万的生成式AI系统提供方，这一门槛实际上覆盖了在该州运营的所有面向消费者的前沿模型厂商。

受管辖的提供方必须在其系统生成的图像、视频和音频中嵌入隐式来源数据，用于标明内容出处与修改历史；同时必须免费提供一个公开可用的检测工具，能读取内容中已有的来源数据并给出结果。此外还须为用户提供可见的显式标注选项。

执法路径是民事诉讼而非监管牌照，罚则为每项违规每日5000美元。对于持续大规模更新的服务而言，这种按日累计的结构会让长期不合规迅速变得昂贵。

## 下一步

AB 853不只是改了日期，它把这套架构从模型提供方扩展到大型在线平台、生成式AI系统托管平台以及拍摄设备制造商，相关义务分阶段生效——托管平台义务自2027年1月1日起。方向很清楚：把来源元数据推向整条链路，从拍下画面的相机到分发内容的平台，而不是让生成模型独自承担全部责任。

## 为什么重要

美国联邦层面至今仍无来源标记标准。2026年6月2日签署的第14409号行政令要求相关机构在8月1日前设计一套面向前沿模型的自愿发布前披露框架；该日期已过，但没有任何内容公开发布，且行政令所述的基准测试流程按设计属于涉密范畴，这套框架未来也可能不会完整对外披露。在联邦标准缺位的情况下，加州再次成为美国生成式内容标注的事实规则制定者。加上同日生效的欧盟义务，全球两个最大的消费级AI监管市场现在要求同一套底层管线：生成时即嵌入密码学或元数据形式的来源信息，并提供公开的核验方式。这是硬性的工程要求，而非政策表态，且适用于面向全球提供服务的模型。
